key_insight: NbC-reinforced Cr3C2-NiCr HP-HVOF coatings can replace WC-based systems, with wear behavior controlled more by microstructure and carbide–matrix bonding than by hardness alone.
engineering_relevance: CrNbC and FeNbC maximize hardness and dense coating formation, while NiNbC offers the best abrasive wear resistance despite lower hardness, giving designers a tunable route for severe-service coatings.
method: HP-HVOF sprayed Cr3C2–25NiCr coatings with NbC-based additions (NiNbC, CrNbC, FeNbC)
Characterized microstructure and phases using coating morphology and XRD
Compared hardness and abrasive wear performance across the three reinforcement chemistries
evidence_signal: The abstract reports dense low-porosity lamellar coatings for CrNbC and FeNbC, XRD evidence of retained NbC plus partial Cr3C2 decarburization, hardness of 945–1003 HV0.3 for CrNbC/FeNbC, and improved abrasive wear resistance for NiNbC.
watch_item: NiNbC showed reduced deposition efficiency and thinner, more heterogeneous coatings, so process optimization is needed before it can be used reliably in production.
paper_title: Microstructure, phase evolution, and wear behavior of NbC reinforced Cr3C2-NiCr coatings deposited by HP-HVOF
